_readme: These are MEASURED baselines, not targets. Each number here was captured by actually
running the named command and reading its output on the date recorded in the entry's
Changing any number in this file is a deliberate act that belongs in the SAME commit as
whatever changed the underlying measurement (a fix, a new test, a dependency bump). This
file is never edited to make a red CI run go green without that accompanying change.
A DROP in a failure count is as much a reason to investigate as a RISE. A failure that
disappeared without a commit that fixed it is a signal, not a free pass — see voteEngine's
exact (not floor) check on both count and titles.
scripts/assert-ci-baselines.mjs reads this file by import.meta.url, never mutates it, and
has no 'update the baseline' mode. Updating a baseline is a human, reviewed commit.

voteEngine.note:
Re-measured 2026-09-01 for the @optimystic 0.24.2 -> 0.25.1 / p2p-fret beta.3 -> beta.4 bump. Live run: 1656 passing / 72 pending / 9 failing.

expectedFailing 8 -> 9. The added title is the THIRD P2P-11 residual tripwire ('no seeding path exists from a circuit-relay reservation into the peer address book'), which flipped on the bump. It is a source-SHAPE tripwire over installed db-p2p, not a behavioural test, and it flipped because 0.25.1 reshaped Libp2pKeyPeerNetwork.findCluster -- classifySelfDialability now splits the old `parsed.length === 0` count into `addressless` vs `selfRelayOnly`. The residual itself is NOT fixed: 0.25.1 still assigns the locally-parsed addresses straight into the record (libp2p-key-network.js:889) and still merely COUNTS addressless members (:886, :895) rather than seeding them. It is carried as a known failure rather than re-anchored because the spec's own sibling test demands a device n=4 re-proof before the assertions are rewritten against a new version -- that proof has not been run. Re-anchor all three P2P-11 tripwires together, after it.

SIX failures were RETIRED in this same commit, which is why 9 is not 15. Three were version pins reconciled to the new line (no-portal-vendor-regression PUB-01-c, and published-stack-lock-regression PUB-02 x2). Three were the gossipsub/libp2p-3 skew tripwires (post-peerId-patch blocker 3), whose subject db-p2p 0.25.1 removed outright -- the block was rewritten from 'the skew still exists' to 'gossipsub is absent and must not return', so the coverage is inverted, not deleted. The dead @chainsafe/libp2p-gossipsub yarn-patch resolution was dropped from root package.json in the same commit; the .patch file is retained on disk.

minPassing 1411 -> 1656 (ciMinPassing 1410 -> 1655). The 1411 figure was measured 2026-08-26 and had gone stale as later waves added tests, leaving the floor ~245 tests loose -- it would not have caught a mass disappearance. Raised to the live measurement here because this is already a reviewed baseline commit. The deliberate ciMinPassing = minPassing - 1 relationship is UNCHANGED and still has the same cause, restated: `.planning/` is a nested git repo the outer repo gitignores, so a fresh CI checkout never has it, and strand-cohort-routing-coverage.spec.ts's 'the diagnosis doc is present...' test calls this.skip() when absent -- reporting as pending on CI instead of passing. expectedFailing stays exactly 9 in BOTH environments; only the passing/pending split moves.

@optimystic 0.25.1 -> 0.27.0 bump (2026-09-03): the baseline is UNCHANGED and was re-measured live, not carried forward -- 1656 passing / 72 pending / 9 failing, and assert-ci-baselines.mjs vote-engine emits RECEIPT passing=1656 failing=9. All nine knownFailureTitles are still red for their own reasons; none was retired and none was added, so minPassing/ciMinPassing/expectedFailing all stand.

The bump did move ONE test passing -> failing before it was reconciled: no-portal-vendor-regression PUB-01-c pins the de-vendored @optimystic/db-* line and read '0.25.'. It was re-anchored to '0.27.' (the @serfab half stays '0.11.' -- cadre-core was deliberately NOT bumped to 0.12.0, see below), together with published-stack-lock-regression PUB-02's two 0.25.x assertions. That is the same version-pin reconciliation this note records for the previous bump; it is not new coverage and not a relaxation.

@serfab stays at 0.11.0 ON PURPOSE. cadre-core 0.11.0 declares @optimystic/db-p2p ^0.24.0, so an npm-shaped install would nest an unfixed 0.24.x behind it; the root `resolutions` flatten it instead -- `yarn why @optimystic/db-p2p` shows every consumer, cadre-core included, on one 0.27.0 copy and yarn.lock has zero 0.24.x/0.25.x @optimystic entries. cadre-core 0.12.0 would remove that nesting hazard at the source but is a BREAKING change (relays move from network.listenAddrs to a new network.relayAddrs, and the old shape is rejected at construction), which packages/p2p-probe-host/relay-smoke.mjs, relay-multi-peer-smoke.js, tools/multipeer-gate/repro/probe-holders.mjs and vote-engine/test/relay-reservation-coverage.spec.ts all still encode. That migration is deliberately a separate change.

NOT caught by this suite, or by any test: @optimystic/db-p2p 0.27.0 ships a static class block in dist/src/storage/block-latch.js, which @react-native/babel-preset does not transform. It breaks the RELEASE BUNDLE of both RN apps -- Authority via `yarn build` (:app:createBundleReleaseJsAndAssets FAILED), Voter with no gate at all, since the Voter workspace has no build script. Fixed by listing @babel/plugin-transform-class-static-block in both babel.config.js files. Proven in both directions with --reset-cache on the Voter: without the plugin the bundle dies on block-latch.js, with it a 15.0 MB bundle writes clean. NOTE the trap -- the first negative control ran WITHOUT --reset-cache and passed, because metro served the cached transform from the successful run; a metro-cache false negative reads exactly like 'the file is not in the graph'.

@serfab 0.11.0 -> 0.12.0 + quereus 4.17.1 -> 4.18.0 bump (2026-09-03): baseline UNCHANGED and re-measured live -- 1656 passing / 72 pending / 9 failing, RECEIPT passing=1656 failing=9. All nine knownFailureTitles still red for their own reasons.

This bump is CHAINED, not optional: cadre-core 0.12.0 requires @quereus/quereus ^4.18.0, so @serfab cannot move without quereus moving, which forces a forward-port of the datetime-immediate-check-coercion patch. That port was NOT verbatim -- it grew from four files to five. 4.18.0 added runtime/emit/write-coercion.js, a WriteCoercionNode placed in the row-expansion projection UPSTREAM of emitInsert, so the row now arrives already converted and disabling the emitters' own coercers no longer restores 4.3.1 semantics. Measured: the four old edits alone left 73 failing (49 of them `CHECK constraint failed: SubmittedAtValid`); adding the write-coercion edit returned the suite to its floor. Fully UNPATCHED 4.18.0 is 1395 passing / 265 failing with 224 in-class (4.17.1 was 1396/264 with 225). update.js also needed re-derivation: upstream replaced the row-level `coerceGenerated` with a per-cell `generatedCoercions` Map, so 'disabled' is now an EMPTY MAP and stays inert only while the `if (coerce)` guard survives.

THREE version-pin locks were re-anchored (reconciliation, not relaxation): no-portal-vendor-regression PUB-01-c (@serfab half now SPLIT -- strand-proto stays 0.11. because 0.12.0 was never published for it, cadre-core and quereus-plugin-sereus move to 0.12.), and published-stack-lock-regression UPG-06's two quereus assertions (exact version and patch locator), with 4.17.1-831db23a51 added to the superseded-locator list.

TWO relay red-locks were REPOINTED, and this is the part that mattered: relay-reservation-coverage.spec.ts and strand-cohort-routing-coverage.spec.ts both PINNED the shape cadre-core 0.12.0 now REJECTS -- a relay-qualified `<relay>/p2p-circuit` entry in network.listenAddrs on a control node. They were GREEN while the app code they guard would have thrown at CadreNode construction on 0.12.0 ('network.listenAddrs names a relay directly ... Move the relay to network.relayAddrs'). Both now assert the relayAddrs shape and assert the retired one ABSENT; discrimination proven by reverting apps/VoteTorrentAuthority/src/providers/CadreNodeProvider.tsx to the old shape (9 -> 13 failing) and restoring it.

COVERAGE GAP found while proving that, still OPEN: both relay locks read only apps/VoteTorrentAuthority. The Voter's CadreNodeProvider.tsx carries the identical relay config and is covered by NEITHER -- reverting it to the fatal shape leaves the suite green at 1656/9. Not closed here (out of scope for a dependency bump); it is why the app-side break was invisible in the first place.

relaySmoke.note: PUB-03 (Node half) — the phase 40 requirement that packages/p2p-probe-host/relay-smoke.mjs reaches a live /p2p-circuit reservation ('RELAY SMOKE: PASS') on published @serfab/cadre-core. This was 40-VALIDATION.md's only manual-only, zero-automated-sampling requirement; scripts/assert-relay-smoke.mjs closes that gap. Measured live 2026-09-01 on Node v22.15.0 against the CURRENT published substrate (@serfab 0.11.0, @optimystic 0.25.1, quereus 4.17.1 -- already moved well past the 0.8.1/0.14.1/4.3.1 versions the requirement text names): 6 consecutive runs (3 bare `node relay-smoke.mjs`, 3 through the wrapper) all PASS at 1.8-2.2s wall each, reservation observed via getMultiaddrs()/p2p-circuit at a consistent ~1.26-1.3s. relay-smoke.mjs's own internal RESERVATION_TIMEOUT_MS is 30000ms; hardTimeoutMs=60000 in the wrapper gives headroom over both figures for a slower CI runner while still bounding a genuine hang. This entry is a discipline record only -- scripts/assert-relay-smoke.mjs hardcodes HARD_TIMEOUT_MS inline (not read from this file) because assert-ci-baselines.mjs's five subcommands are all log-parsers over a captured run, and relay-smoke.mjs is instead spawned and asserted directly by its own wrapper; there is no 'relaySmoke' subcommand here. Discrimination proof (both directions, 2026-09-01): the wrapper was pointed at three fixture scripts standing in for relay-smoke.mjs (never relay-smoke.mjs itself, which was not modified) -- (a) prints 'RELAY SMOKE: FAIL' + exits 1 -> wrapper exit 1, correctly caught by the FAIL-marker branch; (b) exits 0 with NEITHER marker -> wrapper exit 1, correctly caught by the missing-marker branch (proves the exit code alone is not trusted); (c) prints nothing further and hangs, ignoring SIGTERM -> wrapper's SIGKILL fired at the (temporarily lowered, for test speed) timeout and exit 1. All three were RED as expected; the real relay-smoke.mjs run immediately after was re-confirmed GREEN, so the gate is not stuck red.
